_about: What Allelio must report for examples/example_23andme.txt. Checked by tests/test_example_recall.py against a small database built from the real ClinVar/GWAS/gnomAD rows for these rsIDs (tests/fixtures/example_*), and by scripts/check_example.py against a full local database. 'reported' is whether the site appears in the default results (no --include-benign); 'category' is checked only where ClinVar drives it (GWAS-only categories depend on which association loads first); zygosity fields are checked wherever present.

rs28897696.why: BRCA1 pathogenic (expert panel), one copy; ClinGen curates BRCA1 for a dominant (cancer predisposition) and a recessive (Fanconi anemia) condition, so one copy is not demoted to carrier status

rs113993960.why: CFTR F508del (ATCT>A), written DD in 23andMe's I/D notation and matched by allele length: two copies, the affected genotype for cystic fibrosis (ClinGen: autosomal recessive, Definitive)

rs76763715.why: GBA1 N370S, one copy. ClinGen curates GBA1 for Gaucher disease (recessive) and Parkinson disease (dominant), so gene-level inheritance is mixed and the site stays a health condition with that note

rs334.why: HBB sickle-cell T>A, one copy (sickle-cell trait); the T>G likely-benign row at the same rsID must NOT be the one reported

rs1800562.why: HFE C282Y, one copy. ClinGen curates HFE only for a recessive condition (hemochromatosis type 1, Definitive), so one copy is carrier status, ordered a tier below the affected genotype

rs3918290.why: DPYD*2A drug response (fluoropyrimidine toxicity), one copy

rs1042713.why: ADRB2 salmeterol response; the degenerate G/G benign row at the same rsID must be ignored; ClinPGx adds a level 2A salmeterol annotation for the AG genotype

rs12913832.why: HERC2 eye colour association, two copies

rs4988235.why: MCM6 lactase persistence association, one copy

rs1805007.why: MC1R R151C, conflicting classification, one copy

rs1805008.why: MC1R R160W, conflicting classification, two copies; ClinVar lists the gene as MC1R;TUBB3 and only the first gene is consulted for inheritance (TUBB3's dominant curation is about a different condition)

rs9939609.why: FTO, GWAS-only site, one copy of the risk allele A

rs9923231.why: VKORC1 -1639G>A, one copy. ClinPGx level 1A annotation for warfarin dosing, shown with the annotation text written for the CT genotype

rs4149056.why: SLCO1B1 c.521T>C, one copy. ClinPGx level 1A annotations for statin-related myopathy; a level-3 simvastatin note at the same site is below the default evidence cutoff and is not shown

rs7412.why: APOE: reference CC carries no copy of the ClinVar drug-response T allele (set aside), but GWAS associations reported for the C allele remain, two copies

rs429358.why: APOE e4, conflicting classification; one copy but common (AF 16%) so the frequency adjustment pushes it past the benign cutoff. Visible with --include-benign.

rs1799945.why: HFE H63D, conflicting classification, common (AF 10%): same as above

rs1042714.why: ADRB2, benign; its only row is not allele-specific

rs1800497.why: ANKK1 Taq1A, benign, and homozygous reference

rs6025.why: Factor V Leiden absent: CC carries no copy of the ClinVar drug-response T allele, so that row is set aside, and the degenerate C/C conflicting row is ignored. But the GWAS Catalog also reports associations for allele 'G' at this site, which is the opposite-strand name for the reference C (ClinVar says the site is C/T); Allelio infers the flip, counts 2 copies, and flags the call 'read on the opposite strand'.
